The Challenge

Two days a month, rebuilding the same report

Every month HR exported the employee master, cleaned it, rebuilt a dozen pivots, recounted headcount, diversity, tenure and age, and redrew the charts for leadership. The steps never changed; only the month did.

Time drain

Building the monthly HR report by hand took two full days, so insight reached leaders late.

Error avalanche

Manual counts, filters and copy-paste put the integrity of vital HR data at risk every cycle.

Inefficiency overload

The laborious routine drained productivity and crowded out strategic HR initiatives.

Many cuts of one data

Geography, grade, gender, tenure, age and talent landscape all had to agree, and checking that by eye was slow.

HMC Approach

Record the routine once, then let VBA run it

Built inside the HR team's own workbook, so nothing new had to be installed or learned.

Select a step to see what happened.

Discover · Watch one cycle

We sat with the HR analyst through a full monthly build.

  • Logged every step, from the HRMS export to the final charts.
  • Found where time and errors came from: name fields, filters, recounts.
  • Listed every number leadership actually read.

Deliverable: Step map with time and error hotspots.

Design · One MIS sheet, one dashboard

The export lands in an MIS sheet; everything else is generated.

  • Month selector drives every count (joiners, leavers, tenure, age).
  • Fixed bands: tenure, age group and grade groups.
  • Built-in checks so the totals always reconcile.

Deliverable: Dashboard layout and band definitions.

Build · The FinalHM macro

A single macro rebuilds the report from scratch.

  • Concatenates names, deletes and recreates the PivotTable sheet.
  • Builds the pivot cache, pivots and charts in order.
  • Runs reconciliation checks and flags any mismatch.

Deliverable: Kamal Solution VBA.xlsm with modules and a RunMacro sheet.

Adopt · Paste, pick, run

The first live month ran side by side with the manual report.

  • Paste the export into MIS, choose the month, press Run.
  • Both versions matched; the manual one was retired.
  • A one-page guide on the RunMacro sheet.

Deliverable: Parallel-run sign-off and guide.

Scale · New cuts, same button

New views became additions to the macro, not extra hours.

  • Talent landscape by SBU and function.
  • Brazil and India views in one run.
  • Charts module separated so new visuals plug in.

Deliverable: Modular code: Mod_Final, Mod_FinalCharts, Mod_FinalSnippets.

    Key Takeaways

    What any HR team can borrow

    01

    If the steps repeat, record them

    A routine that is the same every month is a macro waiting to be written.

    02

    Rebuild, don't patch

    Deleting and recreating the pivots each run means no stale filters or leftovers from last month.

    03

    Put the checks in the code

    When totals reconcile automatically, review time goes into reading the numbers, not checking them.
